instruction: As observed on 9 September 2026, start from the 2020 Nature Medicine article "Single-cell landscape of bronchoalveolar immune cells in patients with COVID-19" (doi:10.1038/s41591-020-0901-9). Identify the GEO series generated by that study, distinguishing it from healthy-control data borrowed from another study. The complete candidate universe is Europe PMC records indexed with that series in ACCESSION_ID, with OPEN_ACCESS:Y and IN_PMC:Y, and FIRST_PDATE from 13 May through 31 December 2020 inclusive. These are catalogue field criteria, not an unrestricted keyword search or citation search. Within this universe, identify papers that actually reanalyzed or integrated the seed study’s cell-level expression/count matrix, and that also generated a distinct experimental transcriptomic or mass-spectrometry proteomic dataset deposited in GEO, ArrayExpress, or ProteomeXchange/PRIDE. Report every qualifying paper–deposit pair. Only study-level accessions explicitly identified in the paper as deposited experimental data count (GSE, E-MTAB, or PXD); input datasets, computational derivatives, software, on-request data, and prospective deposits without assigned identifiers do not qualify. A deposit already associated with and reported as experimental data in a different, earlier journal article is not newly generated for the candidate paper, even if the candidate’s resource table labels it "this paper". Use repository publication links and the earlier article to resolve such provenance; a preprint or another version of the same work is not a different study. A paper may reuse an input dataset and contribute another new dataset: judge each accession separately. Multiple repositories or accessions for one dataset must not produce duplicate records; use the GSE, E-MTAB, or PXD study identifier explicitly cited in the candidate paper.
output_format: Return only a pipe-separated table with header pmcid|deposit_accession. Use canonical PMC and study accession identifiers. Sort lexicographically by pmcid, then deposit_accession.
